business_problem: Guardian Life needed to modernize expensive, siloed financial systems and limited analytics tools so finance teams could automate more work, get deeper insight into policy and tax data, and avoid maintaining multiple aging on-premises platforms.
solution_summary: Guardian Life consolidated financial management on Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM, Oracle Fusion ERP Analytics, and Oracle Accounting Hub to create one source of financial truth. Transaction and policy-related data flows into the Oracle platform instead of remaining spread across PeopleSoft and other legacy systems, allowing finance, FP&A, and tax teams to work from the same dataset. Oracle Cloud EPM automates tax data collection, journal entries, and calculations, while Oracle Accounting Hub applies rules to transform transaction information into detailed accounting entries. Oracle Fusion ERP Analytics adds KPIs, machine learning, and drill-down capabilities so users can analyze trends at the policy-holder and geography level instead of stopping at surface-level reporting. The shared platform cut total cost of ownership, accelerated access to new functionality through quarterly updates, and gave teams more time for insight generation instead of system maintenance.

Oracle Fusion Cloud Enterprise Performance Management (EPM)

data_flow: Financial, tax, policy, and transaction data now flows into Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP and EPM instead of isolated legacy systems; Oracle Accounting Hub standardizes accounting entries, and Oracle Fusion ERP Analytics reads from the consolidated data set to surface KPIs, trends, and drill-down analysis for finance teams and adjacent business functions.
business_outcome: Guardian Life went live in nine months, reduced total cost of ownership, automated tax and accounting work, and gave finance teams faster access to deeper policy- and geography-level insights from one cloud platform.
